subject: [PATCH 0/5] iomap: remaining patches for iomap_iter_next conversion

reviews.author: Christoph Hellwig
reviews.summary: Christoph Hellwig noted that the patch series did not include a new iomap user (ext4 iomap buffered I/O) in the relevant lists, but otherwise found the conversion to be good.
reviews.raw_body:
Hmm, it would have been nice to CC adding a new creative iomap use
to the relevants lists..

Anyway, the conversion looks good:

Reviewed-by: Christoph Hellwig <hch@lst.de>

2026-10-28.patch_summary: This patch series converts various filesystems to use the new iomap_iter_next model, which replaces the legacy ->iomap_begin() and ->iomap_end() functions. The patches are rebased on current mainline and include preparatory patches for nilfs2 and fuse iomap code. The changes also update documentation to reflect the new model. The series applies cleanly to both current mainline and next-20261027, but conflicts may arise by the time it is picked up at the end of the merge window.

reviews.author: Ryusuke Konishi
reviews.summary: Reviewer Ryusuke Konishi acknowledged the patch as an intermediate step and found its changes to be good, including the finalizing conversion in patch 4/5.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne,

Thanks for picking up the newly merged NILFS2 iomap code and handling
the additional conversion to complete this series.

While this patch is an intermediate step, the changes look good to me,
including the finalizing conversion in patch 4/5.

Acked-by: Ryusuke Konishi <konishi.ryusuke@gmail.com>

Thanks,
Ryusuke Konishi

reviews.author: Joanne Koong (author)
reviews.summary: Author confirmed that the patch series still applies cleanly to both current mainline and next-20261030, addressing concerns about conflicts with other pending changes.
reviews.raw_body:
I pulled in Linus's latest tree (commit abf8c33470f7) and the series
still applies cleanly with no conflicts. It also applies cleanly on
top of next-20261030, which includes the remaining btrfs, ntfs, exfat,
ext2, and gfs2 changes that haven't been merged yet. There shouldn't
be any conflicts between this series and anything else going in this
window.

Thanks,
Joanne
